name: Peresh
overview: Peresh was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh, known primarily as the son of Machir and Maacah. His identity is established in the genealogical record of 1 Chronicles 7:16, situating him within the lineage of Manasseh. There are no additional notes or detailed narratives about his life beyond this familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Peresh means 'offal eviscerated; dung; contents of stomach [not intestine]' in Hebrew. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:16 and was not given by God, reflecting a literal meaning without further biblical title or significance.
familyAndRelationships: Peresh is explicitly identified as the son of Machir and Maacah according to 1 Chronicles 7:16. It is inferred that Ulam and Rakem are his ancestors, likely his forefathers, also referenced in the same verse. Scripture does not provide additional family details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Peresh's significance lies in his placement within the genealogical record of the tribe of Manasseh, which preserves the lineage important to Israel's tribal history. His mention helps establish the continuity of the Manasseh family line, contributing to the biblical emphasis on heritage and God's providential care over His chosen people. Though not a prominent figure in narrative events, his inclusion underscores the value Scripture places on genealogical records.
